topic: Someone finds their grandmother's engagement ring in a pawn shop
text: The rain was coming down like it was trying to wash the whole city away, and there I was, knee-deep in what was supposed to be a quick in and out. The guy on the other end of the line had a voice like a scratched record, telling me about a ring. A grandmother's ring, he said, sitting pretty in a pawn shop on the wrong side of town. I've seen enough grit to know when things are off kilter. This wasn't just some lost treasure. It was a story waiting to spill out, and I was the only one willing to listen. The rain kept pounding as I took another drag, wondering how much more I could take before I hit the bottom. But I've always known how to hold my ground. I told the guy I'd check it out, but I wasn't making any promises. This city eats promises for breakfast.
